    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

    Industry observers note that U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.).

    It has been revealed that megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The Newly introduced York Times has reported.

    The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the firm’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly stated, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

    Industry observers note that by early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the tech giant he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

    It has been revealed that the U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American firm, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

    As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

    Nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress noted that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.

    It has been revealed that “We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stated. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”.

    Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the firm is not considering reinstating Huang. Kress also said that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

    Jensen Huang posted his first public statement since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.

    “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.

    Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.

    Industry observers note that over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an….

    More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

    Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”.

    Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is remarked to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

    In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) mentioned they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

    “Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

    That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

    “The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

    According to recent reports, after Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

    Nvidia remarked its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

    Recent findings suggest that harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

    Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

    “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important organization to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast stated to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”.

    The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

    In a recent development, after reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly intends to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

    Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The organization has not had an obvious successor or a succession strategy.

    The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

    According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

    According to recent reports, huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar remarked Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

    The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

    In a recent development, alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

    It has been revealed that nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

    In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

    On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and revealed support for the Nvidia CEO.

    Sources indicate that “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump mentioned.

    When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”.

    Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

    Industry observers note that “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”.

    Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”.

    “Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our firm. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

    Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

    Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

    Recent findings suggest that “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The glitch of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”.

    U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the Fresh York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

    An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

    “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”.

    U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the Latest York Times.

    Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

    Around the same time, per the Fresh York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

    The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

    Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

    Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

    Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.

    These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”.

    “NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson stated at the time.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (477 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Testing confirms presence of etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.
    • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • Three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised in New South Wales after using certain vapes have tested positive for the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate, health officials said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Testing confirms presence of etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.

    Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

    Three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised in New South Wales after using certain vapes have tested positive for the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate, health officials said.

    NSW health on Friday issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.

    The three people who were hospitalised had used non-nicotine refillable vapes, the state health department stated. Testing of their blood and urine confirmed the presence of etomidate.

    The department would not confirm how old the three patients were, where they were hospitalised, or their condition on Friday.

    The discovery of etomidate in vapes in NSW comes about four months after Victorian health officials declared they had found the powerful anaesthetic agent in an illicit vape sold in Melbourne.

    On Friday, NSW health warned vapes sold as space pods, space oil, kpods, piu piu vapes, or zombie vapes may contain etomidate, or other substances, including ketamine, THC and potent opioids.

    The medical director of the NSW poisons information centre, Dr Darren Roberts, mentioned etomidate’s effects were unpredictable when used in a vape.

    Roberts noted etomidate could cause confusion, drowsiness, slow breathing, vomiting, muscle spasms or movements that were hard to control, and people who took it could become unresponsive.

    These effects could be life threatening, especially if used with other drugs that could cause sedation, such as alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines, and GHB, Roberts said.

    He stated etomidate could also cause long-term harm when used regularly, including the disruption of hormones produced by the adrenal gland.

    These hormones are important in regulating stress responses and need to be replaced if they aren’t produced naturally, he remarked.

    “The contents found in non-nicotine vapes vary,” Roberts said. “You can’t assume what’s inside.”.

    He urged anyone considering using a vape to ask themselves what could be in it.

    Sources indicate that “You won’t get into trouble for seeking medical care,” he said. If you feel unwell, or if your friend feels unwell, after using a vape, do something about it.”.

    NSW health officials mentioned it recommended people administer Naloxone to anyone who became responsive after using any drug, in case they had ingested opioids.

    Naloxone is an opioid overdose treatment, which is free at pharmacies and does not require a prescription.

    Naloxone won’t reverse the effects of etomidate, as the sedative does not belong to the opioid class of drugs, but it is still safe to give, health officials said.

    The officials noted anyone who witnessed someone experiencing unexpected symptoms after using drugs should call triple zero immediately or seek urgent medical attention.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S.
    • In a recent development, the program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base.
    • The Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities as the company tests whether there’s a market for shuttling tweens without an adult by their side. The program, called Uber Kids, debuted quietly over the past few weeks in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin.

    In a recent development, the program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base. Uber is describing this as a limited pilot program, which means it may never expand beyond these cities or even exist by next year. But if successful, it could open up a potentially lucrative market for Uber: busy families with active kids.

    The Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers. Parents or guardians are the only ones who can order a ride for their child, which they can do by adding the child to their family profile and completing a mandatory onboarding that explains the built-in safety features. A parent or guardian must be present at the pickup locations for the trip to begin and also have to include a note to the driver that explains the drop off.

    Meanwhile, only highly rated drivers who have been invited are allowed to participate. Those drivers are required to complete an education module that includes step-by-step instructions and must be opted into live video streaming so parents can watch the trip in real time, according to Uber.

    Uber noted it also requires PIN verification for every Uber Kids trip, and notes all recordings will be encrypted and not available to the driver, and will use sensors and GPS data to detect if the ride goes off course, stops unexpectedly, or ends early.

    Drivers who are willing to adhere to those rules to shuttle kids will get a pay bump for the effort, according to Uber. Eligible drivers will earn $7 more on every Uber Kids trip compared to a standard one, the company indicates on the dedicated Uber Kids web page. Drivers will receive an extra $20 for the first Uber Kids ride they complete.

    The extra compensation underscores a key challenge Uber faces as it expands into this younger age group — how to convince drivers to take on that added responsibility. If the program does expand it could eventually compete with existing transportation services such as HopSkipDrive and Zum.

    Recent findings suggest that uber opened its ride-hailing service to minors in 2023 when it launched Uber for Teens, although the company had conducted early pilots several years prior. As the program expanded nationwide, Uber introduced a live video streaming feature.

    Here's a roundup of the biggest headlines in Germany on Friday, November 20:.

    Police in the German state of Saxony say they deployed water cannons to Leipzig and used them on individuals who repeatedly shot fireworks at officers there after a large demonstration ended.

    Police say roughly 2,500 people took part in a demonstration organized by the group Gen Z Takes Charge, far fewer than the estimated 7,000 who joined the first of these on October 31 (see entries below).

    German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday confirmed that Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani had pledged €15 billion ($16.5 billion) in upcoming German defense and technology investments.

    During a Berlin press conference with the emir, Merz said, "This strengthens both of us, particularly in future technologies such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and aviation.".

    The Qatar-Germany collaboration is aimed at improving security and defense projects that also include defending against cyberattacks, with Merz saying, "We are particularly open to new partnerships in the defense industry.".

    That cooperation comes as both nations look to beef up defenses amid regional conflicts with global consequences.

    The chancellor and the emir also stressed the fundamental importance of diplomacy in the resolution of conflict, with the two leaders' focused largely on Iran and the Middle East — and the need to get the flow of shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz closer to pre-war levels.

    The emir called for deescalation, saying, "We are convinced that true political resolution is the only way to achieve lasting peace.".

    Industry observers note that merz added that the two agreed on the war in Ukraine, saying: "Russia must stop its time-wasting diplomatic games. Moscow has to finally sit down for real peace negotiations.".

    Merz was straightforward on Iran, saying Germany wants peace in the Middle East because it needs affordable energy.

    He later called out Russian maritime marauding on the Black Sea, labeling it a threat to global food security.

    The German broadcaster Sky TV — not to be confused with the British-based Sky Sports F1 which is the largest English-language commercial F1 broadcaster — will not be sending any staff to the Formula 1 Qatar Grand Prix because of security concerns in connection with the conflict in Iran and the wider Middle East.

    Sky TV announced the move on Friday, just a week before the contentious race weekend from November 27-29.

    Sky will broadcast the entire race weekend as usual, but will use global feed images and will not send any of its own staff to Lusail International Circuit.

    F1 races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia this spring were canceled as the US war with Iran was in its most active phase, with major disruptions to commercial flights.

    The season-ending double header in Qatar and then the United Arab Emirates a week later has been in serious doubt ever since.

    Nominally at least, both races are going ahead — and in all likelihood, teams will have already started dispatching equipment and personnel to the region to begin preparations by now.

    Sky TV noted it still planned to send a team to the season finale in Abu Dhabi, just across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, on December 6.

    But it mentioned it continued to "monitor developments and assess the situation on an ongoing basis.".

    Organizers of the Gen Z Takes Charge protest group spoke out about why they took to the streets again.

    Co-organizer Akram Selo called on Germany's leadership to meet the young people's demands.

    "Talks won't make us stop demonstrating," he told RBB-Inforadio in comments aired on Friday.

    According to recent reports, "Essentially, our demands should be addressed, and we should be given assurances. That is what needs to happen, not empty promises," Selo added.

    Sources indicate that "So far, we feel that we aren't being taken seriously at all," he said. "The way we're being treated suggests that the aim is to sideline our demands and discriminate against us by focusing on other trivial matters.".

    Another group, the alliance "School strike against conscription" held its own protest to demand an immediate halt to surveys about potential availability for the German Armed Forces, or Bundeswehr, that are at the moment non-binding and only obligatory for teenage boys.

    German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Ukraine must ‌continue ⁠to ⁠push ahead swiftly with reforms, particularly ​on the rule of ​law and tackling ​corruption, ‌if it hopes to receive a prerequisite for further financial ‌aid and investment.

    Merz made the comment at a ‌business ​summit in Berlin that was organized by the German Chamber of Industry and Commerce.

    "It is now essential to press ahead with these reforms swiftly and resolutely —particularly, and I say this openly, with regard to the rule of law and corruption," Merz told attendees.

    The German chancellor remarked that sustained reform efforts by Kyiv ​were necessary to justify long-term Western support ⁠for ​Ukraine, adding ​that Germany would ​step up ‌its backing in defense and humanitarian ​aid ⁠as Russia intensifies attacks on ⁠Ukraine's ​energy infrastructure ahead of winter.

    "What we invest in Ukraine now, we will receive back many times over as dividends in the form of stability, export opportunities, joint projects, and growth," the German chancellor stated.

    According to recent reports, "Freedom and security are now unleashing forces of progress and resilience on a scale never seen before. This is precisely the stance we are now taking against the autocratic and imperialist actors of this world. We are the world of freedom," Merz added.

    Sources indicate that at home, Merz has faced increasing pressure to justify Germany's ongoing support for Ukraine. In recent regional elections, political parties opposing sending military aid have performed well.

    Merz argued that Russia's war against Ukraine is an attack on democratic values everywhere.

    Germany's electricity exports rose in the first three quarters of this year, according to official data released on Friday.

    According to the energy association BDEW, Germany has been a net importer of electricity since 2023.

    The neighbouring countries Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands, were the most vital buyers of German electricity in the first nine months of 2026.

    Together, they bought about half of all German electricity exports.

    Industry observers note that the volume of German electricity exported rose by 25.5% compared with the same period last year, to 48.8 terawatt-hours, while its value increased by 51.3% to €4.3 billion ($4.7 billion). Electricity imports into Germany fell by 13.3% in volume, but at 49.2 terawatt-hours they remained slightly above exports.

    While imported electricity cost an average of €116 per megawatt-hour, 39% more than a year earlier, exported electricity from Germany averaged only €87 per megawatt-hour, some 20.6% more than a year earlier.

    With a high share of renewable energy sources, wind and solar, Germany tends to offer electricity when supply is high and prices are low, but in times of shortage it has to pay higher prices for imported electricity.

    Finance Ministry officials mentioned they are launching a dialogue process, dubbed "Germany 2035," to develop proposals for the future of the country's economy.

    Officials want to study how Germany can secure growth and prosperity and what that could look like in terms of fiscal policy.

    Finance Minister Lars ​Klingbeil will begin the dialogue process on December ​2, when he welcomes economists from around the world to Berlin.

    Additionally, think tanks, research organizations, universities and civil society groups have been asked to host workshops, which would take place in the first half of 2027.

    Among 12 economic topics that the ministry seeks to explore are tax and fiscal policy, investment ⁠and ​domestic demand, industrial policy, energy ​and climate transition, foreign trade and sovereignty, and housing ​and local infrastructure.

    The dialogue will culminate in a white paper, to be published in 2028, that can provide recommendations for Germany's economic future up to 2035.

    A group called "Gen Z Takes Charge" (Gen Z regelt) has called for thousands of young people to demonstrate in many German cities.

    The gathering comes almost three weeks after the first major youth protests hit Germany, inspired by the protests that took place in France in the last weeks.

    Those protests, which took place on October 31, saw tens of thousands take to the streets across Germany, with crowds remaining largely peaceful, although rioting broke out in several cities, including Frankfurt, later in the evening.

    Among the demands of the "Gen Z Takes Charge" group are increased funding for schools, addiction support and psychotherapy, affordable living, opposition to conscription and consistent action on climate change.

    Another group, the Federal Pupils' Conference, has also organized its own demonstration at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, with police saying that some 5,000 people have already signed up.

    The pupils' conference advocates for improvements in education policy in Germany, including school renovation, school social work, relief for teachers and the inclusion of climate action in curricula.

    The demonstrations are set to begin in the morning and run until late afternoon.

    Steinmeier will also host a state banquet for the emir and his delegation in the evening. Al Thani is also expected to meet with Chancellor Friedrich Merz during the day.

    In a recent development, the visit comes in the midst of tensions in the Middle East, with the war in Iran likely to be a critical topic in the talks between the two governments. Qatar is right now one of the mediators in the deadlocked conflict between the US and Iran.

    Economic and bilateral relations are also expected to take center stage.

    On Saturday, the emir will visit Germany's most populous state of North Rhine-Westphalia, where he will be greeted by its state premier Hendrik Wüst at the military section of Cologne/Bonn Konrad Adenauer Airport.

    During the visit, Al Thani and North Rhine-Wesphalia leaders will hold an economic conference in the small city of Königswinter, near Bonn, where the Emir will also visit Drachenburg Castle.

    Following a political summit on Ukraine in Berlin yesterday, the German Chamber of Industry and Commerce (DIHK) stated it would host a German-Ukrainian business forum.

    Chancellor Friedrich Merz and German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche are expected to be in attendance, along with Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi, among others.

    Christian Bruch, deputy chair of the Eastern Committee of the German Economy and chief executive of Siemens Energy, mentioned German companies are committed to invest in Ukraine, despite Russia's ongoing war and were open to expand their business partnerships.

    Bruch noted bilateral trade was expected to rise to around €13 billion ($14.1 billion) in 2026.

    German flagship airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its airport hubs in Frankfurt and Munich, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

    The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa Airlines CEO Jens Ritter and four other managers.

    The timeframe of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were apart of a previously confirmed downsizing.

    In September 2025, Lufthansa remarked it would slash 4000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

    Lufthansa's parent organization Lufthansa Group had 67,100 employees in Germany by the end of last year. In the letter seen by news agencies, Lufthansa said financial struggles were the reason behind the planned cuts.

    "Lufthansa is currently not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter said, while pointing out that the tech giant operated at a €180 million ($197 million) loss in the first nine months of this year.

    In addition, Lufthansa Airlines is now in its third straight year of being unprofitable.

    In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

    Leaked documents raise upcoming questions about Deutsche Bank's dealings in Russia up to Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, adding to scrutiny over the bank's risk controls and past controversies.

    Breaking: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a latest threat is rising: the teals

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns.
    • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • The Upcoming South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns.

    Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

    The Upcoming South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.

    This time, the threat is from independent candidates – and they’re backed by the same community activists who put a swathe of teal independents into federal parliament.

    The challenge, which has so far remained under the radar, comes as the NSW Coalition tries to shore up its right flank against a surging One Nation before the March state election. This has resulted in the Coalition lurching to the right on issues ranging from gun control to law and order, and, in the case of the NSW Nationals, to abandon climate targets altogether.

    As former opposition leader Mark Speakman resigned from the Liberals on Thursday – joining an exodus of MPs announcing they wouldn’t contest their seats in March – he warned his party against becoming “One Nation lite”.

    But the move to the right has also created an opportunity for progressive independents running in urban seats usually held by Liberal moderates, with several candidates about to launch their campaigns.

    This weekend, Amelia Loye, a management consultant who specialises in stakeholder and community engagement, will announce she is running in the seat of Willoughby, on Sydney’s north shore. She will attempt to oust Liberal MP Tim James, who holds the seat on a 2.6% margin.

    Loye is backed by community group Willoughby Votes, which came close to securing an independent in the 2023 election with 47% of the two-party preferred vote.

    “Willoughby has already shown it is ready for an independent,” she said. “Nearly half of voters backed one last time. I want to earn their support, and the support of those still deciding.”.

    She joins high-profile candidate Elouise Massa, a small business owner, who became a household name after campaigning for Northern Beaches hospital to return to public hands after her toddler’s death in emergency.

    Massa will run in the Sydney seat of Manly against Liberal Adelaide Cuneo, who is seeking to replace the retiring MP, James Griffin.

    Industry observers note that the independent deputy mayor of Mosman, Michael Randall, announced last weekend he will run in North Shore as a community independent. Several of the people behind former independent federal MP Kylea Tink’s campaign are supporting him.

    Monica Wulff, another independent, has announced a run in Davidson.

    Voters on the northern beaches have already sent two independents to Macquarie street – and both have a good chance of being returned.

    At the federal level, teal independents Sophie Scamps, Zali Steggall and Nicolette Boele hold McKellar, Warringah and Bradfield respectively. Tink held North Sydney for one term before the seat was abolished.

    The NSW Liberal party is not giving up on the northern beaches and the north shore, despite the trend towards independents.

    “We’ll keep making our case directly to voters, including why we oppose Labor’s gun buyback that targets law-abiding owners rather than criminals and terrorists,” a Liberal spokesperson mentioned.

    This time, however, the independents have a boost in the form of NSW Labor premier, Chris Minns.

    Recent findings suggest that during the final weeks of parliament before the NSW election, Minns joked that independent Jacqui Scruby, who won Pittwater at a byelection, should be known as “the member for Mona Vale road” for her tenacity in seeking an upgrade. It’s now being fast-tracked by the Minns government.

    Minns has also appeared with Massa, and praised her for her advocacy.

    But Minns, a shrewd political operator, has not fallen in love with independents – he’s just hedging his bets.

    Sources indicate that A year ago, with the Liberals languishing in the polls, Labor could have expected to increase its majority in 2027. But with One Nation storming to a primary vote as high as 30% in some polls, that prospect has dimmed.

    In the current parliament, Labor has support of three independents – Greg Piper, Joe McGirr and Alex Greenwich – to ensure confidence and supply for its minority government. An expanded crossbench would give more options and provide a buffer for Labor losses to One Nation in western Sydney, the Hunter and possibly the Central Coast.

    If all independents were successful – and that is a massive if – almost the entire north shore region would go to state independents, except the seat of Wahroonga.

    Most of the commentary about the 2027 election has focused on the likely Armageddon facing the Nationals, who could lose as many eight or nine of their 11 seats in the regions.

    But a teal wave also remains a threat to the Liberal party, especially as the Coalition try to position themselves to fight off One Nation in the regions with policies that don’t sit well with urban voters.

    One Nation could also prove helpful to independents if it makes good on its promise to run candidates in every seat. The party is more likely to shave votes from the Liberal primary vote, making it easier for the independents to overtake the Liberal on preferences from Labor and the Greens.

    NSW’s optional preferential voting makes it hard to predict how strong flows will be – and it depends what parties advocate on how to votes. But in 2023 only 41% of One Nation voters nominated preferences, compared to 70% of Green voters and 49% of Labor voters.

    The opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, has not ruled out either a preference deal or a post-election arrangement with One Nation, describing such options as “hypothetical”. But if they do end up preferencing One Nation, it may alienate moderate Liberals and ultimately work against them.

    Disclosure: Anne Davies worked as a media and policy adviser to the independent federal MP Sophie Scamps from October 2023 to October 2024.

    Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.
    • "Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".
    • They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.

    "Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".

    They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.

    Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks.

    Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen, south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One.

    In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.

    Putin claimed Russia was not against the idea but said Moscow wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".

    Industry observers note that "That is why, through diplomatic channels, we have invited the Europeans to come to Moscow in order to determine their positions. And after that, we will decide in what format we will continue the dialogue with Ukraine.".

    But Putin also stated that "every day" Russia heard that European leaders were talking about war coming in 2030. "But we are not planning to attack anyone... Is that normal? I do not think so," he said. Still, Putin added, Russia understood that "discussing challenges linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans".

    Jared Kushner told reporters that the US president had come away from Shenzhen believing that "peace is achievable".

    Striking an upbeat note, Kushner stated that the Russians were willing to trust the instinct of the US envoys "on our behalf" that the Europeans should be at the table and that Moscow was now "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on the idea enshrined in Nato's Article Five that requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack.

    Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who also was at the summit in Germany's capital, has long sought a guarantee equivalent to Nato's collective defence clause, and there has been little indication that Putin would accept that kind of condition.

    Russia rejects outright the idea of Ukrainian membership of Nato, but reports say US negotiators have mulled the idea of giving Kyiv Article Five-style guarantees without being part of the Western defensive alliance if it agrees to painful territorial concessions.

    Zelensky and the three European leaders â Merz, Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron â were not as upbeat as Kushner, and the Ukrainian president made clear that the Russian president had spurned every proposal so far: "Putin has always remarked no.".

    The German chancellor was equally sceptical, although he remarked with US involvement the chance of peace was increasing. Europe was willing to enter "serious discussions on European security" with Russia, he explained, "as long as it's matched with a serious discussion and only first a peace agreement with Ukraine".

    "These talks have to begin, and we will accept if conditions are acceptable for Europe and Ukraine," remarked Merz.

    He also mentioned any attempts to divide Europe into spheres of influence run by major powers was unacceptable, amid concerns on the continent that this problem may have been on the agenda at the trilateral talks in Shenzhen.

    Analysis: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance.

    "A 'Yalta format' will not bring peace," Merz mentioned, referring to the post-World War Two agreement between the US, the USSR and Britain in 1945.

    He also sought to downplay the Shenzhen summit as above all "a photo opportunity.".

    "The US understands that there can be no peace without us. We, in turn, know that with the United States by our side, the prospects for peace increase," Merz added.

    Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also took exception to Trump's description of Putin as a "friend" at the Shenzhen summit, saying: "Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be.".

    Meanwhile, Macron urged Ukraine's allies to do the "maximum" to deliver the much-needed air defence systems Kyiv needed to repel deadly Russian attacks.

    The French leader also urged the allies to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's membership in Nato.

    There have been mixed messages from Moscow on European participation to the talks. Last week, following a visit to Moscow, the US envoys, Steve Witkoff and Kushner, appeared certain that Europe would soon have a seat at the negotiating table.

    But the Russians were more circumspect and this week Putin's aide Yury Ushakov stated a "great deal" would have to be done before the format could be expanded, suggesting that several more rounds of discussions would have to be held before any four-sided talks could take place.

    Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

    Several buildings were damaged in the latest Russian attack on Ukraine's capital Kyiv.

    While Russia has engaged with several rounds of talks over the last year, little in Moscow's rhetoric or actions suggests that the Kremlin is considering scaling down its war on Ukraine.

    It continues to pound Kyiv's energy infrastructure to cripple it as winter takes hold, increasing numbers of civilian casualties are being recorded across the country, and Kremlin officials have not budged from Russia's demands for Ukrainian sovereign territory.

    According to recent reports, as delegations were meeting in China and Germany on Thursday, several buildings in Kyiv's historic centre came under attack from drones. One person was killed in a strike on a residential building in the Podilskyi neighbourhood, while the Dutch and Austrian embassies as well as Saint Volodymyr's Cathedral reported damage.

    And Putin also vowed that Moscow's response to a Ukrainian strike on the Crimean Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea would be "considerably more painful" than what Kyiv had achieved.

    He also noted he had discussed a "possible ceasefire in a number of areas" but had decided against it after the attack on the bridge.

    Still, Putin claimed to be "interested" in ending the war and was ready to make compromises, while Ukraine and Europe were not.

    "I assure you, we have no desire at all to continue this armed conflict," Putin noted, despite the fact that Russia has in recent months intensified its attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure as cold winter approaches.

    Kyiv and its European allies say that â in the absence of any major success on the vast front line â the Kremlin leader is seeking to break Ukrainian resistance by leaving millions of civilians without electricity and water supply.

    #12566. These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (983 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

    These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, it’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms.
    • Sources indicate that apple Pay went down.
    • The first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms. In the past two weeks, the U.S.’s top businesses have faced technical outages that have disrupted the systems that run everyday life.

    Sources indicate that apple Pay went down. NASA’s internal communication network went down. The FAA had to ground all flights for hours (only the third time in history since 9/11), and Microsoft was hit with an outage that took down Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for nearly two days.

    The first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago. Here in the U.S., the director of National Intelligence said these outages don’t seem related to state-sponsored terrorism, while President Trump called the challenges “individual events.” Many of the companies themselves have said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks or AI attacks, but tech issues.

    Only, there’s the fact that they all struck within a short timespan of each other, and just a few weeks after Cybersecurity’s so-called “Black October,” when a slew of also-unrelated cybersecurity incidents occurred on October 21, striking PHP, Node.js, LiteLLM, more.

    While there’s no reason to view these outages as cyberattacks, there may be more than coincidence going on: It’s giving AI-native Y2K, frankly.

    Dave DeWalt, an investor who worked in cybersecurity for more than three decades (including as president and CEO of McAfee and as vice chairman of the CISA Advisory Council for the Department of Homeland Security), also thinks it’s probably AI-related.

    The technical outages are most likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” and that “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before through AI tools like Mythos and others,” he told TechCrunch.

    It has been revealed that the thing is, many of these technical flaws have always existed, but because AI is surfacing them so fast, enterprises are rushing to fix them before bad actors can exploit them. “That surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he remarked.

    This was, perhaps, the first moment when legacy meets modern, Anusha Iyer, a software engineer and founder of the security startup Corsha, told TechCrunch. “These industrial systems were never designed to be connected, let alone securely connected in the way we are pushing them to be today,” she mentioned.

    Virginia Senator Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intel Committee, came to a similar conclusion (although investigations are still underway as to what could be happening). “These disruptions should serve as a wake-up call. It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” the senator wrote on X.

    Recent findings suggest that AI is reshaping how software is built, deployed, and operated, on a scale where everyone feels the sharp learning curve. Iyer cited the FAA outage as an example of legacy tech that is not as sophisticated or advanced as the technologies companies are trying to merge it with.

    In less technical terms, she said the outage may have been caused (and preliminary findings point to this) when the FAA was trying to modernize its telecommunications infrastructure and the transition overwhelmed parts of its legacy hardware, where the fresh tech likely operated at a normal modern capacity while the legacy hardware couldn’t keep up.

    When looked at this way, she said, AI is actually getting the bad rep. “It’s not rapid adoption of AI yet causing these outages,” she said. “The fault is the rushed mix of the legacy and modern systems without a clear understanding of operational and cyber risk or the ability to gatekeep and protect the legacy systems.”.

    Organizations need a more steadfast approach to AI adoption, including more testing and prioritizing what needs to be fixed and when, DeWalt said.

    Iyer added, “These industrial systems need to be segmented more tightly and more access controlled, so as modern systems are introduced, it can be phased in and risk mitigated.”.

    Industry observers note that actually, there might be a silver lining to all of this for companies (and for venture investors). DeWalt noted he’d rather see these U.S. enterprises find and patch their flaws, even in this messy way, than have bad actors find and exploit those vulnerabilities in AI warfare that could cause even more national security issues.

    In a recent development, and maybe some aspiring founders were inspired by them. DeWalt expects a rise in companies focused on “AI-driven vulnerability management, autonomous remediation, safe patch testing and deployment, and resilience for the systems that keep critical infrastructure running,” he remarked.

    “There’s real pain in this transition as we’ve seen in the past week,” DeWalt remarked. “But there’s also enormous opportunity for the companies that help organizations move at AI speed without breaking things.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • GTA+ adds a few perks to GTA 6 and one of them is already stirring up players.
    • In a recent development, A lot has changed in gaming in the 13 years since Grand Theft Auto 5 debuted.
    • It has been revealed that that $8 gets you a few perks in GTA 6, but nothing game-changing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    GTA+ adds a few perks to GTA 6 and one of them is already stirring up players.

    In a recent development, A lot has changed in gaming in the 13 years since Grand Theft Auto 5 debuted. That includes the explosion of live-service games and gaming subscriptions, and the Grand Theft Auto franchise has gotten in on both with GTA Online and the GTA+ membership. Now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, GTA+ members get some additional benefits in the upcoming game on top of what the subscription already offers in GTA Online.

    It has been revealed that that $8 gets you a few perks in GTA 6, but nothing game-changing. You'll get 10 percent more money for any eligible vehicles you sell in the game and a 10 percent discount at a variety of stores. You can also use in-game transport options like scooters, bikes and public transit for free and get a premium membership to the RydeMe rideshare service. Together, those perks add up to a few cheaper ways to get around GTA 6's huge map and an easier time making cash. That can make a big difference in your progress early in the game, since cheats don't unlock until you beat the story.

    Industry observers note that the biggest and most controversial benefit is one you can claim only after reaching GTA 6's third chapter. At that point, you'll get the '90 Annis Venturas BLVD Elegy, a free sports car, plus a garage in the Crosstown area. Locking exclusive items in a single-player game behind a monthly subscription is never popular, and players have already voiced their displeasure on Reddit.

    For most players, the GTA+ subscription fee probably isn't worth it for what it adds to GTA 6 alone. From the start, GTA+ has focused mostly on GTA Online, giving members in-game currency and discounts, new vehicles and garages to store them in, and a rotating suite of items and features. For dedicated GTA Online players who also picked up GTA 6, there's a much better case for the subscription.

    The game library included with GTA+ might make it worth it for more people. Anyone with an active subscription also gets access to a selection of Rockstar's other games, including Red Dead Redemption and GTA 5. Of course, you might not have time for any of those until you finish a campaign that can run 80 hours, but the library does make the $8 subscription much easier to justify.

    Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide, proposing medical support instead of prosecution for those who survive.
    • The proposal seeks to shift Nigeria's approach from criminal punishment to treatment and rehabilitation.
    • It follows years of calls for reform from mental health professionals.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The bill has been proposed by Nigeria's president.

    Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide, proposing medical support instead of prosecution for those who survive.

    The proposal seeks to shift Nigeria's approach from criminal punishment to treatment and rehabilitation.

    It follows years of calls for reform from mental health professionals. A separate bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide has already passed its second reading in the Senate.

    Under Nigeria's law, attempted suicide is a criminal offence with those convicted facing up to one year's imprisonment, a fine or both.

    The Senate bill also seeks to replace criminal penalties for attempted suicide with medical treatment, rehabilitation and support.

    It was sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, who has argued that prosecuting people who survive suicide attempts could discourage those experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help.

    He also warned that families might conceal such incidents for fear of prosecution and social stigma.

    He stressed that the bill is not aimed at legalising or encouraging suicide attempts but rather protecting the survivors.

    Tinubu's proposal has been welcomed by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, who had previously suggested that people who survived suicide attempts should be sent to prison.

    "We are saying that suicide is a crime for now. Therefore, if you attempt it, we will send you to prison," Akpabio had remarked.

    However, after receiving the Tinubu's proposal, he sought to clarify his earlier remarks, saying they did not apply to people experiencing mental health conditions.

    He added that punishing people whose actions were influenced by mental health conditions would be insensitive.

    Tinubu's letter follows sustained calls from mental health professionals for the law to be changed.

    At a parliamentary public hearing in May 2024, the then president of the Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria, Professor Taiwo Obindo, urged lawmakers to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide.

    "Why do we, as a nation, then punish individuals who are ill and need medical attention rather than prosecution?" he asked.

    Drawing on his experience as a psychiatrist, Obindo stated most people who die by suicide have a history of mental illness.

    Akpabio has referred the president's amendment bill to the relevant senate committee for further consideration.

    Nigeria is among several African countries where attempted suicide remains a criminal offence.

    Ghana decriminalised attempted suicide in 2023, while Kenya's High Court ruled in January 2025 that the law criminalising it was unconstitutional.

    #12561. Latest page in history? Xi, Trump and Putin summit was more of a footnote

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (900 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theguardian ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest page in history? Xi, Trump and Putin summit was more of a footnote

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Far from the grand ambitions declared in Yalta in 1945, Shenzhen felt like a meeting in search of an agenda.
    • It is arguably true, given it was the first such meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US, that Thursday’s gathering in Shenzhen deserved the description of “historic”.
    • But in terms of tangible outcomes, it is unlikely to warrant the “fresh page in the history of diplomacy” that Vladimir Putin claimed had been written, and will instead be consigned to a smallish footnote in any future volume of the 21st century.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Far from the grand ambitions declared in Yalta in 1945, Shenzhen felt like a meeting in search of an agenda.

    It is arguably true, given it was the first such meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US, that Thursday’s gathering in Shenzhen deserved the description of “historic”.

    But in terms of tangible outcomes, it is unlikely to warrant the “fresh page in the history of diplomacy” that Vladimir Putin claimed had been written, and will instead be consigned to a smallish footnote in any future volume of the 21st century.

    According to recent reports, it’s true that the meeting could yet be an icebreaker and the start of a permanent newly introduced dialogue. It’s also true that each leader can return home with something from the 90 minutes they spent together.

    Despite falling asleep during the main Apec summit, Donald Trump had a chance to show his proximity to two authoritarian leaders he admires. With Ukraine having destroyed Russia’s bridge into Crimea, the US president greeted Putin as not just a friend but almost a wartime ally.

    The Russian president, although occasionally pushed to one side by protocol during the early photo opportunities, will be able to show back home that it is Moscow, and not his adversary Europe, let alone Ukraine, that commands the respect and attention of Trump and Xi Jinping. As such, the summit was a free gift to Putin, and underlined that Trump was no longer the leader of the free world, as the former British foreign secretary Jeremy Hunt commented.

    From Putin’s perspective, a meeting in Berlin of the coalition of the willing was a sideshow. Europe’s attempts to isolate Russia had failed and the Asia-Pacific region had become the centre of the global economy, Putin boasted. His relationship with Trump, he said, despite the difficulties, was founded on “similar civilisational values”.

    It has been revealed that for Xi, it was a prestigious chance to play host and implicitly demonstrate that the era of American hegemony is over. No longer the sole arbiter in world affairs, the US, the consumer economy, must share the stage with China, the manufacturing giant, and Russia, the energy bank.

    The trio’s brief joint statement covered four pretty disparate topics: boosting energy supply, reforming the United Nations, limiting the powers of the international criminal court (ICC) and a tentative commitment to discuss nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation.

    For grandeur at a time of various global crises, these ambitions hardly matched Yalta in 1945 or even the declaration after the Tehran summit in 1943, when the leaders of the UK, US and the USSR sat on the veranda of the British embassy and pledged that their countries would work together after the war to build a “world family of democratic nations” free of tyranny and oppression. Winston Churchill declaimed in Tehran: “In our hands we have the future of mankind.” Joseph Stalin went further. “History has spoiled us,” he said. “She has given us very great power and very great opportunities.”.

    Shenzhen, by contrast, felt like a meeting in search of an agenda. The vacuum was filled with platitudinous commitments to “maintain strategic stability and international security”, a task that – looking around the world – none of those in attendance are presently pursuing with great effect.

    It has been revealed that perhaps technology, multipolarity and their own divisions mean even they do not have “very great power”. Certainly there were no accompanying intends for how to reform the UN, let alone boost energy production or show respect for international law – a subject Trump’s current favoured successor, Marco Rubio, had just disparaged in a speech as a plaything of the global elite.

    In a recent development, it was the summit’s chief instigator, Putin, who was the most eager of the three to set the meeting in a historic context, describing China, Russia and the US as the victors of the second world war, in a deliberate slight to Britain. A pledge to “preserve and strengthen the system of international law” seemingly referred to ensuring certain world leaders were freed from the prospect of the ICC serving them with arrest warrants.

    Industry observers note that by coincidence, the other world court, the international court of justice (ICJ), found a state – Myanmar – guilty of genocide for the first time on the same day. The Shenzen statement did not name the ICJ as a target, beyond an oblique reference to the ICC and “other similar institutions”. Doubtless that is only because ICJ rulings can be dismissed with near impunity.

    Industry observers note that xi, nervous that China’s status as protector of the global south might be damaged by being involved in a global superpower carve-up, stuck to a familiar script: “History tells us that when major powers are at peace, the world is secure. When they clash, there is chaos.”.

    It may be that behind the scenes, or at other events, serious progress is being made on how China might act as a guarantor of a peace deal with Iran, or on who should lead the UN through its coming phase of reform, or even on how Putin might bring himself to seek peace in Ukraine in a way that protects Ukrainian sovereignty.

    For the moment, though, it looks as if what little history was made in Shenzhen was made for exclusively the wrong reasons.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Meta looks to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the manufacturer’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported.
    • When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Meta looks to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the manufacturer’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported.

    When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.”.

    So far, Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with a variety of cute avatars that users can use to give the system more of a personality.

    Muse Charm, the company’s push into AI hardware, will allow users to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands.

    Recent findings suggest that it remains to be seen whether customers will bite or not. AI wearables have had a rough go of it so far (here’s looking at you, Humane Ai pin), but companies continue to iterate on the concept in an attempt to break through to a broader audience.

    Indeed, $300 is arguably a pretty steep price for a product the size of a keychain, although it’s also a price point that’s in line with what other companies have been charging. The wearable debuted by Friend — the AI startup whose device lets you text and talk to an AI persona — is at the moment retailing for $250. On the other hand, Amazon’s all-new Bee Frontier wearable AI device — which transcribes conversations and tracks tasks — lists for $75 and is currently on a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49. Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user’s apps (photos, emails, etc.), it’s still far less expensive than Muse Charm.

    #12557. Rocket Report: A weekend of ups and downs; Stoke celebrates engine milestone

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1973 w)
